history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. Can you help me get it working again?

I can help you troubleshoot your phone’s service and picture messaging issues. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account
- Your customer ID
- Your full name and date of birth

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the steps to restore your service.
Sure, my phone number is +1-617-555-0148 and my name is Sofia Martinez.

Thank you, Sofia. I have your account details. To help restore your service and picture messaging, I’ll guide you through some quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, can you confirm if Airplane Mode is off and your SIM card is inserted properly? If you’re not sure, I can walk you through checking these settings. Would you like step-by-step instructions?
I'm not sure, could you please walk me through how to check if Airplane Mode is off and if my SIM card is inserted properly?

Let’s check both settings step by step:

1. Airplane Mode:
 • Look at the top of your phone’s screen (the status bar). Do you see an airplane icon?
 • If you do, Airplane Mode is ON. You’ll need to turn it OFF. Usually, you can swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings and tap the airplane icon to disable it.

2. SIM Card:
 • If Airplane Mode is off and you still have no service, your SIM card might not be detected.
 • To check, you can usually go to Settings > About Phone > SIM Status (or similar, depending on your device).
 • If it says “No SIM” or “SIM not detected,” your SIM card may need to be reinserted.

Would you like me to guide you through these checks using diagnostic tools on your phone? If so, please let me know, and I’ll provide the next steps.
Yes, please guide me through these checks using diagnostic tools on my phone.

Great! Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar for Airplane Mode and signal status, and then we’ll check your SIM card status. Please follow the prompts on your device as I guide you.

First, let’s check your status bar for Airplane Mode and signal indicators. Please run the diagnostic tool to check your status bar. Let me know what you see, or if you need instructions on how to access this tool.
I checked the status bar and it shows 'No Signal', but I do see the Data Enabled icon and it says 'Connected to Chestnut-5G'. There’s no airplane icon.

Thank you for checking. Since there’s no airplane icon, Airplane Mode is off, which is good. However, seeing “No Signal” means your phone isn’t connecting to the cellular network, even though mobile data is enabled and you’re connected to Wi-Fi.

Next, let’s check your SIM card status to see if it’s being detected properly. Please use your phone’s diagnostic tool to check the SIM status (usually found in Settings > About Phone > SIM Status, or similar). Let me know what it says—does it show “Active,” “Missing,” or “Locked”? If you need help finding this, let me know!
I checked the SIM status and it says 'active.' So the SIM card is being detected, but I still have no service or signal bars.

Thank you for confirming that your SIM status is “active.” Since Airplane Mode is off and your SIM is detected, but you still have no signal, the next step is to check your network settings—specifically, your Access Point Name (APN) settings, which are crucial for connecting to the cellular network.

Could you please check your APN settings on your phone (usually found in Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Access Point Names)? Let me know if you see any unusual entries or if the APN looks incorrect or empty. If you’re unsure, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default. Would you like to proceed with resetting your APN settings?
Yes, please guide me through resetting my APN settings to default.

To reset your APN settings to default, please follow these steps:

1. Go to Settings on your phone.
2. Tap on Network & Internet (or Connections).
3. Select Mobile Network.
4. Tap on Access Point Names (APN).
5. Look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings” (usually found in the menu, which you can access by tapping the three dots in the upper right corner).

After resetting your APN settings, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like me to guide you through rebooting your device now?
I reset the APN settings to default and got a message saying the settings were reset and I need to reboot the device for the changes to take effect. Should I go ahead and restart my phone now?

Yes, please go ahead and restart your phone now. This will apply the new APN settings and may restore your cellular service and picture messaging functionality.

Once your phone has restarted, check if you have signal bars and if you can send or receive picture messages. Let me know the results, and if you still have issues, I’ll guide you through the next steps.
My phone rebooted successfully and the settings changes were applied, but I still have no signal bars and can't send or receive picture messages. What should I try next?

Your line status is active on our end, and there are no suspensions or contract issues. Since your SIM is detected and your APN settings are correct, the next thing to check is your network mode preference.

Please check your phone’s network mode setting (usually found in Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Preferred network type). Is it set to 2G, 3G, 4G, or 5G? If it’s set to 2G or 3G, try changing it to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G.” Let me know what you find or if you need help with this step.
I checked my network mode preference and it's already set to '5G preferred.' Still no signal bars and nothing loads.
YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.

arguments.summary: Customer Sofia Martinez has no cellular service (no signal bars, nothing loads, cannot send/receive picture messages). SIM is active, line is active, APN settings have been reset and applied, network mode is set to 5G preferred, and all standard troubleshooting steps have been completed. Advanced technical support is required.
